title: Miles on Rubin: experimental BF16 container bringup
summary: Started from the native ARM64 SGLang CUDA 13.4 image, preserved its Torch and CUDA-dependent runtime, rebuilt the training extensions against that environment, and validated specific BF16 training and rollout paths on SM10.7. This is an experimental recipe, not a claim that upstream Miles supports every Rubin workload.

image.architecture: linux/arm64; aarch64 CPU; Rubin compute capability 10.7
image.runtime_source_note: Later experiments mount separately recorded Miles source commits. The image digest does not identify the mounted runtime source; each experiment must report both.

comparison_caveat: The GB300 performance experiment uses the upstream Miles container, as requested. Rubin uses this custom CUDA 13.4 container. These are not identical software environments: CUDA, Torch, native packages and patches must be listed alongside the results. A measured runtime gap includes software-stack differences and cannot be attributed solely to GPU hardware. The older VeRL run is a historical learning-curve reference, not the current performance control.

components.name: CUDA / Python / Torch
components.action: Retained from the upstream cu134 ARM64 base
components.rationale: Replace the audited cu130/Torch2.13 wheel assumptions with extensions matching the selected cu134 Torch environment.
components.validation: Base ABI snapshot and selected native package versions checked during build; installed versions read again from the preserved runtime image.

components.name: cuDNN / NCCL / CuTe DSL
components.source_ref: Pinned cu134 base; frontend version pinned in the Rubin recipe
components.action: Retained base native libraries; installed the pinned cuDNN frontend
components.rationale: Avoid mixing CUDA-library or Torch ABI versions. Added the pip cuDNN include/library directories to compiler search paths.
components.validation: Selected TE/cuDNN small-shape forward/backward and NCCL tests passed. Qwen3.5 THD d256 cuDNN backward failed; the underlying cause was not established.

components.name: FlashInfer / SGLang native packages
components.version: flashinfer-python 0.6.18; flashinfer-cubin 0.6.18; flashinfer-jit-cache 0.6.18+cu134; sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1; sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post2+cu134; sgl-deep-ep 0.1.0+cu134
components.action: Retained; not rebuilt by the Miles recipe
components.rationale: Preserve the rollout kernels already built for the selected Torch/CUDA environment.
components.validation: SGLang FlashInfer backend import and two offline BF16 decode shapes passed against FP32 SDPA, maximum absolute error 0.00136. This does not validate every FlashInfer or DeepEP/DeepGEMM path.

components.name: SGLang Python source
components.version: Editable distribution metadata 0.0.0; identify by commit, not that version string
components.action: Pinned source checkout; reconciled dependency metadata to the retained native versions; editable install with --no-deps
components.rationale: Keep Miles-specific SGLang behavior while preserving the cu134 native dependencies.
components.validation: Actual rollout paths passed in the recorded Qwen3.5 runs. Unused Rust/TreeCore and other optional paths are not covered.

components.name: Transformer Engine
components.action: Built from source with NVTE_CUDA_ARCHS=107a, NVTE_FRAMEWORK=pytorch and NVTE_WITH_NCCL_EP=0
components.rationale: TE 2.19 adds upstream Rubin support; source compilation matches the selected Torch ABI.
components.validation: TE Linear and FusedAdam checks passed. Attention validation is configuration-specific; the release-level support statement is not proof that every backend, head dimension or packed layout works.

components.name: Apex
components.action: Built C++/CUDA extensions from source for TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.7; replaced explicit C++17 flags with C++20
components.rationale: Avoid reusing cu130/Torch2.13 CUDA wheels with a different Torch build.
components.validation: FusedAdam update compared against Torch Adam in the component smoke.

components.name: FlashAttention 2
components.action: Built from source; patched setup.py to emit compute_107/sm_107 and use C++20
components.rationale: Supply FA2 kernels built for Rubin and the selected Torch headers. The FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS=100 recipe selector enters the upstream branch whose actual target is explicitly patched to 107.
components.validation: Direct FA2 and TE-wrapped FA2 forward/backward passed on SM10.7 for three no-gap THD BF16 d256 test cases; output/gradient relative L2 error versus FP32 reference was below 0.31%.

components.name: Megatron-LM
components.action: Pinned editable source install with --no-deps; builds the CPU pybind dataset helper
components.rationale: Preserve the Miles training fork while deliberately selecting TE 2.19 separately. This Megatron pin does not itself pin or certify TE 2.19; its dependency metadata is older.
components.validation: Actual Megatron actor, optimizer and weight-sync paths passed in the recorded two-node BF16 Qwen3.5 runs.

components.name: mbridge / Torch Memory Saver
components.action: Pinned source installs; force-reinstalled the TMS CUDA 13 library using TMS_CUDA_MAJOR=13
components.rationale: Use the exact Miles dependencies in the new runtime. TMS was rebuilt even though the base exposed the same package version.
components.validation: TMS preload library present; actual colocate/offload workflow passed. The experiments use raw weight conversion, so installing mbridge is not a validation of its bridge/LoRA paths.

components.name: Qwen3.5 Gated DeltaNet dependencies
components.version: fla-core 0.5.2; flash-linear-attention 0.5.2; inherited tilelang 0.1.12 and triton 3.8.0+gitdf3f91dd
components.action: Added both FLA distributions with --no-deps; selected FLA_CONV_BACKEND=triton and FLA_DISABLE_BACKEND_DISPATCH=1
components.rationale: The split FLA packages are needed for both fla.modules and gated_delta_rule imports. Causal-conv1d was not needed for the selected Triton path.
components.validation: Imports and actual Qwen3.5 GDN training passed. Standard Qwen3-30B-A3B does not use this GDN path.

components.name: Python runtime dependencies
components.source_ref: Actual preserved Rubin image metadata; final freeze in /opt/miles-rubin
components.action: Resolved Miles requirements under native constraints; restored setuptools 80.9.0 after the Megatron build
components.rationale: Megatron build metadata needs setuptools<80, while inherited ModelOpt requires >=80. Version 80.9.0 satisfies the runtime constraint and still supplies pkg_resources.
components.validation: Build imports and direct Miles requirements passed. ModelOpt's presence does not mean QAT/quantization paths were tested.

changes.title: Preserve the native base before resolving Python dependencies
changes.detail: Snapshot and constrain 40 native package versions plus the Torch ABI before resolving Miles dependencies.
changes.explanation: The check covers selected package versions and the Torch CXX11 ABI, not byte-for-byte hashes of every library.

changes.title: Rebuild training extensions; retain rollout extensions
changes.detail: Rebuild TE, Apex, FA2 and TMS in the core image; retain the cu134 rollout stack and use a Python-only TE patch in the final increment.
changes.scope: Core native compilation versus incremental package/Python changes
changes.validation_status: PASS for the recorded component and model tests
changes.explanation: FLA packages are added with --no-deps; the final increment does not recompile the core native libraries. Runtime Triton JIT compilation is a separate matter.

changes.title: Scoped TE eligibility patch for Qwen3.5 d256
changes.detail: Allow only the numerically tested SM107 BF16/d256/dropout0 FA2 case through TE’s existing dispatch checks.
changes.scope: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B only in these experiments. Current Qwen3-30B-A3B uses head dimension128 and does not require this d256 exception.
changes.validation_status: Direct and TE-wrapped FA2 numeric probes PASS; recorded no-gap Qwen3.5 end-to-end runs PASS; forced-gap layout remained NoBackend
changes.explanation: Observed TE/cuDNN backward failure: No valid execution plans built for causal THD BF16 d256, GQA 8:1, dropout 0. Unpatched TE also rejected FA2 via a head-dimension allowlist. The patch adds only CC10.7 + BF16 + Q/K/V dimension256 + dropout0 to that eligibility condition; all other backend checks remain. It changes Python dispatch, not CUDA kernels, and does not establish the cuDNN failure's root cause.

changes.title: Remove an incompatible inherited FA4 beta
changes.detail: Remove the inherited FA4 beta because its CuTe imports are incompatible with the retained DSL4.8 package.
changes.scope: Selected image packaging; FA4 and FA3 are unused
changes.validation_status: Selected FA2 and rollout paths validated; alternative FA4 configurations untested
changes.explanation: The base FA4 beta imported CuTe APIs unavailable in DSL4.8, and TE imported the installed package eagerly. Removed flash-attn-4 and its SGLang dependency declaration. This was an observed package/API incompatibility, not evidence that every FA4 version is limited to Blackwell or cannot run on Rubin. Hopper-only FA3 was not added.

changes.title: Runtime fixes are separately tracked
changes.detail: Track MNNVL environment settings and the checksum diagnostic repair separately from the native image build.
changes.scope: Experiment configuration and runtime source, not a general container support claim
changes.validation_status: Recorded two-node transport and learning checks PASS
changes.explanation: Two-node runs kept NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 and NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0 to obtain MNNVL with colocate/offload. A later Miles checksum diagnostic fix mapped optimizer-owned native FP32 shards correctly; it did not change attention kernels or training math and was delivered as mounted source, not a replacement native image.

validated: Core build: actual Miles actor import, TMS CUDA13 library, BF16 GEMM, TE Linear backward, TE/Apex Adam numerical checks, FA2 forward/backward, selected TE/cuDNN attention, four-GPU NCCL all-reduce and two FlashInfer decode shapes.
Registry provenance: core and incremental images retained by manifest digest; final image push/API verification and two-node pulls passed.
Qwen3.5 execution smoke: real rollout, optimizer execution, offload and three all-rank synchronizations passed. Its zero rewards and gradients only establish execution.

Qwen3.5 learning validation: two-node BF16 TP2/EP8 with two TP4 rollout engines passed two updates with independently recomputed rewards, nonzero gradients, changed served tensor hashes, matching engines and three all-rank synchronizations.
The later Qwen3.5 GSM8K/1K comparison also passed its terminal collector and learning audit. These are separate results from the current Qwen3-30B-A3B learning/performance experiment.
limitations: No claim of upstream Miles end-to-end Rubin certification, general model coverage, convergence, or unrestricted long-context/backend correctness.

The TE 2.19 release-level Rubin claim and the successful scoped FA2 tests do not imply every TE/cuDNN or FA4 configuration works. Rubin is not restricted to cuDNN: the tested FA2 path executed successfully.
The current Qwen3-30B-A3B curve/performance status must come from its own final logs and collector; this build report does not mark that experiment complete.

Untested optional paths include FA4, FA3, TE NCCL-EP, Megatron-Bridge/LoRA conversion, QAT/quantization, and model-specific optional kernels not exercised by the recorded recipes. TileLang and ModelOpt are installed; presence alone is not validation.
The core build recorded eight pre-existing pip-check warnings from the upstream base and no newly introduced warnings; direct Miles requirements and selected imports passed.
GB300 uses an upstream Miles container and Rubin uses this custom image. Record both actual software manifests; performance results are a comparison of hardware plus runtime stacks.
